feature.title: Cancer Vaccine Cuts AML Death Risk 41%, While Surgical Robots and AI Tools Hit Clinical Deployment Milestones Across the Globe
feature.summary: This week in medtech marks a confluence of landmark clinical trial readouts, FDA authorizations with real-world deployment data, and large-scale AI rollouts at major health systems. SELLAS Life Sciences' leukemia vaccine galinpepimut-S delivered a 9-month survival advantage in a Phase 3 trial, while Virtuoso Surgical's endoscopic robot demonstrated 94% intact tumor specimen retrieval post-FDA authorization. On the digital health front, Doximity's AI suite went live across NewYork-Presbyterian's 10-hospital network, and Heartflow's CT-guided PCI planning tool — backed by RCT data published in the NEJM — changed procedural plans in 70% of real-world patients. Vascular closure, robotic endoscopy, and AI-assisted diagnostics round out a dense week of implementation-driven medtech news.

highlights.label: Biggest story
highlights.text: SELLAS Life Sciences' Phase 3 REGAL trial showed leukemia vaccine galinpepimut-S cut death risk by 41% and extended median survival from 14.7 to 24 months in AML patients.

highlights.label: Key trend
highlights.text: AI is moving from benchmarks to bedside: RCT-validated CT-guided PCI planning, real-world ambient scribe rollouts, and FDA-cleared aneurysm detection software all hit deployment milestones this week.

highlights.label: To watch
highlights.text: Virtuoso Surgical's first-in-class FDA-authorized bladder tumor robot is planning a focused US launch at leading urology centers in 2027 following its 94% detrusor muscle retrieval result.

articles.title: SELLAS Cancer Vaccine Cuts Death Risk by 41% in Phase 3 AML Trial
articles.snippet: SELLAS Life Sciences' galinpepimut-S (GPS), a WT1-targeting peptide immunotherapy cancer vaccine, met the primary overall survival endpoint in the pivotal Phase 3 REGAL trial enrolling 126 AML patients in second or later remission. GPS delivered a median overall survival of 24.0 months versus 14.7 months for best available therapy, with a hazard ratio of 0.59 (p=0.035) and no new safety signals.
articles.result: 41% death risk reduction; 24 vs 14.7 month median survival

articles.title: Virtuoso Surgical Robot Wins FDA De Novo Authorization for Bladder Tumor Resection with 94% Detrusor Retrieval
articles.snippet: Virtuoso Surgical received FDA De Novo authorization for its endoscopic robotic system — the first device in a new FDA classification — for en bloc bladder tumor resection through the urethra. In the VIABLE clinical study of the first 20 patients at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, detrusor muscle was present in 94% of resected lesions, exceeding both the prespecified 60% goal and the ~70% historical median for conventional TURBT, with no intraoperative adverse events or 30-day deaths.
articles.result: 94% detrusor retrieval; zero intraoperative AEs in 20-patient VIABLE study

articles.title: Abbott Amulet 360 Achieves 96.3% Complete LAA Closure at One Year in VERITAS Pivotal Study
articles.snippet: Abbott reported one-year results from the 458-patient VERITAS pivotal study of its next-generation Amulet 360 Left Atrial Appendage (LAA) occluder, designed to prevent stroke in nonvalvular AFib patients. Complete LAA closure was achieved in 96.3% of patients evaluated by transesophageal echocardiography, with only a 1.8% rate of ischemic stroke or systemic embolism at 12 months; results were simultaneously published in JACC: Cardiovascular Interventions. The device has CE Mark and FDA approval is pending.
articles.result: 96.3% complete LAA closure; 1.8% stroke/embolism rate at 12 months

articles.title: Heartflow CT-Guided PCI Matches IVUS Outcomes in 1,105-Patient RCT, Published in NEJM
articles.snippet: Heartflow's P4 randomized controlled trial — the largest of its kind, enrolling 1,105 patients across 23 centers in the US, Europe, and Japan — showed CT-guided PCI planning was non-inferior to gold-standard intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) guidance for the primary endpoint of 12-month target-vessel failure (4.1% vs. 4.6%), while cutting median procedure time by 27% and contrast volume by 12%. Real-world NAVIGATE-PCI registry data further showed that Heartflow PCI Navigator changed procedural plans in approximately 70% of patients compared to angiography alone.
articles.result: Non-inferior to IVUS; 27% faster procedures; 70% plan-change rate in real world

articles.title: Tandem Mobi Receives FDA Clearance as World's First Tubeless AID System with 7-Day Wear
articles.snippet: Tandem Diabetes Care received FDA 510(k) clearance for its Tandem Mobi as the world's first tubeless automated insulin delivery system with up to seven days of wear, making it the only insulin pump cleared for both tubed and tubeless infusion. The system uses Control-IQ+ technology to predict glucose levels 30 minutes ahead via CGM readings and automatically adjust insulin, with existing in-warranty Mobi pumps already compatible — no hardware replacement required for current users.
articles.result: First tubeless AID system; 7-day wear cleared; existing pumps compatible

articles.title: Doximity Clinical AI Deployed Across NewYork-Presbyterian, Columbia, and Weill Cornell Medicine's Epic EHR
articles.snippet: Doximity expanded its AI clinical suite — including Doximity Ask (HIPAA-compliant decision support grounded in peer-reviewed literature) and Doximity Scribe (ambient note generation) — to all three major academic medical institutions that together operate 10 hospitals and 450+ care locations across New York City and Westchester, integrating directly into Epic. This followed Doximity adding 25 new AI hospital enterprise clients in a single quarter, with HCA Healthcare's parallel rollout of ambient scribes reportedly saving physicians one to two hours per shift across 100+ hospitals.
articles.result: AI tools live across 10-hospital, 450-location NYP network via Epic

articles.title: Haemonetics VASCADE MVP XL Earns CE Mark; First Commercial Procedures Completed in Germany, Italy, and UK
articles.snippet: Haemonetics announced CE Mark certification today (Nov. 18, 2026) for its VASCADE MVP XL venous vascular closure system, with first commercial European procedures already completed in October at Asklepios Clinic Altona (Hamburg), Centro Cardiologico Monzino (Milan), and Cromwell Hospital (London). The XL device uses 58% more collagen and a 9% larger disc than the existing VASCADE MVP, targeting larger-bore procedures including pulsed-field ablation, cryoablation, and left atrial appendage closure requiring 10–12F sheaths.
articles.result: CE Mark granted; first real-world procedures completed in 3 EU countries

articles.title: Bracco & Avicenna.AI Secure FDA Clearance for UPTUNITY Aneurysm AI Detection Software
articles.snippet: Bracco and Avicenna.AI received dual FDA 510(k) clearances (K262062 and K262147) for UPTUNITY | Aneurysm, a combined computer-aided detection and diagnosis tool that flags suspected saccular brain aneurysms larger than 3mm on head CT angiography and tracks their size over time within the radiologist's existing PACS workflow. The tool is the first product in Bracco's new UPTUNITY clinical decision-support portfolio and will be commercially distributed by Avicenna.AI, with a showcase planned at RSNA 2026.
articles.result: FDA-cleared CADe/CADx for aneurysms >3mm; integrated into existing PACS workflow

articles.title: MedInTech AI Robotic Endoscope INTION S Validates Non-Inferiority in 178-Patient Trial, Raises $25.7M Series C
articles.snippet: Korean startup MedInTech's INTION S motorized robotic endoscope demonstrated non-inferiority in key maneuverability measures versus conventional mechanical endoscopes in a 178-adult clinical trial at Seoul National University Hospital, with significantly reduced clinician physical fatigue — results published in Scientific Reports. The company has since deployed the device commercially to Korea's National Fire Service Hospital, Ajou University Hospital, and started early sales in Thailand, the Philippines, and Mongolia, backed by a fresh $25.7M Series C announced today.
articles.result: Non-inferior to conventional endoscopy; clinician fatigue reduced in 178-patient RCT

articles.title: Patient-Facing AI in Primary Care Passes First Real-World Safety Test: 98 Patients, Zero Safety Stops
articles.snippet: A prospective study published in The Lancet by researchers at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center enrolled 114 patients to interact with a conversational AI system (AMIE) before their primary care visit, with 98 completing the full workflow; none of the 98 conversations triggered a predefined safety stop, only one hallucination was noted, and patient attitudes toward AI improved after the interaction and remained higher after the physician visit. Clinician evaluators and patients both rated the AI conversations favorably across a broad set of communication and safety criteria.
articles.result: Zero safety stops in 98 real-world primary care AI consultations; 1 hallucination

articles.title: Wearable AI Predicts Patient Deterioration 8–24 Hours Before Standard ICU Alerts in Hospital Deployment
articles.source: Stanford Medicine / Nature Communications (via Stanford-Harvard State of Clinical AI Report)
articles.snippet: A hospital-based study highlighted in the 2026 Stanford-Harvard State of Clinical AI Report demonstrated that an AI model trained on continuous wearable vital signs predicted patient deterioration 8 to 24 hours before standard hospital alerts fired, identifying patients at risk for ICU transfer, cardiac arrest, or death while intervention was still possible. Separately, a systematic review in ScienceDirect found AI-driven wearable sensors achieved a 30% ICU reduction via predictive analytics and detected sepsis 2–4 hours earlier in surgical patients.
articles.result: Deterioration predicted 8–24 hrs early; 30% ICU reduction in systematic review
